preconditions.description: The number of necklace parts n is between 1 and 500,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= a < 2**20 and 0 <= b < 2**20 for a, b in parts)
preconditions.description: Each pearl color a and b in the input is a non-negative integer less than 2^20.
The input contains exactly n necklace parts, each represented as a pair of pearl colors.

postconditions.expression: max_beauty == max(beauty for beauty in beauties)
postconditions.description: The first line of output is the maximum possible beauty of a necklace built from all given parts, where beauties is the list of beauties of all possible valid necklaces.
The second line of output contains exactly 2n distinct integers representing the indices of the pearls in the order they appear on the cycle.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= p <= 2 * n for p in pearl_order)
postconditions.description: Each pearl index in the output is between 1 and 2n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(pearl_order.count(i) == 1 for i in range(1, 2 * n + 1))
postconditions.description: Each pearl index appears exactly once in the output.

postconditions.expression: all(abs(pearl_order.index(2 * i - 1) - pearl_order.index(2 * i)) == 1 for i in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: For each necklace part i, the indices of its two pearls (2i-1 and 2i) are adjacent in the output permutation.
The beauty of the necklace is a non-negative integer.

postconditions.expression: beauty == min(beauty_of_connection(u, v) for u, v in zip(pearl_order, pearl_order[1:] + [pearl_order[0]]))
postconditions.description: The beauty of the necklace is the minimum beauty of any connection between adjacent pearls in the cycle, where beauty_of_connection(u, v) is defined as follows: if u == v, beauty is 20; otherwise, beauty is the largest k such that 2^k divides u XOR v.
